clue.text: Front page story to swallow — return of spacecraft

parts.note: a splash is a big story given prominence on a newspaper's front page
to down a drink is to swallow it

explanation.surface: A newspaper is told to gulp down its front-page story about a spacecraft coming home.
explanation.definitionFit: A capsule's landing at sea at the end of its mission is called this, the usual return of early spacecraft.

clue.text: Darling given break to find item of food

parts.note: sugar is a term of endearment like darling
to snap is to break

explanation.surface: A sweetheart is given a rest so they can go and find a snack.
explanation.definitionFit: A sugar snap is a kind of pea eaten pod and all, a vegetable.

clue.text: Left figure facing upwards?

indicators.note: in a down clue, facing upwards means reading from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: nine is a figure or number

explanation.surface: A left-wing leader's statue looks to the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the man: a figure of the political Left, as on monuments gazing upward.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian revolutionary leader was the outstanding figure of the communist Left.

clue.text: Stumble through offensive which proves illuminating

indicators.note: through means one piece runs right inside the other

parts.note: slighting means insulting, offensive
to trip is to stumble

explanation.surface: Falling over during an attack, which turns out to be enlightening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' looks like a military push but is the adjective SLIGHTING; TRIP goes 'through' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluorescent tube lamps give light, so this kind of fitting is literally something illuminating.

clue.text: Stupid officer, one coming into money

indicators.note: coming into means entering, so these pieces go inside the money

parts.note: dosh is British slang for money
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A dim-witted officer inherits a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming into money' reads like an inheritance, but it is the container signal; dosh is British slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Doltish means like a dolt, a dull, slow-witted person, so stupid.

clue.text: Cat favourite, or dog?

parts.note: the cat, short for cat-o'-nine-tails, is a whip
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: Is the household's favourite animal the cat or the dog?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cat' is not the animal but the cat-o'-nine-tails used for flogging.
explanation.definitionFit: A whippet is a breed of slim racing dog like a small greyhound.

clue.text: On reflection, healer given discharge

indicators.note: something seen in a mirror appears turned round, so the word for the healer is read backwards

parts.note: time is the great healer, as the proverb says

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, a doctor is handed a discharge from hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'healer' looks like a doctor but is TIME, from the saying that time heals all wounds; 'On reflection' turns it round to EMIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to give out or send forth, a verb synonym of discharge.

clue.text: New poem encapsulated by wonderful love for grandee

indicators.note: encapsulated by means held inside the next word

parts.note: magic means marvellous, wonderful
If is Kipling's famous poem
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A fresh poem wrapped up in a lovely tribute for a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'encapsulated by' is the container signal; 'love' is nil in tennis, written as the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnifico is a Venetian magnate, hence any grandee or person of high standing.

clue.text: Bird, an enormous thing

parts.note: a tit is a small bird

explanation.surface: A bird, surprisingly a huge creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A titan is a giant, from the gigantic deities of Greek myth.

clue.text: Blanket is rank

definitions.meaning: as an adjective, blanket means covering everything, all-inclusive

explanation.definitionFit: General means applying across the board, like a blanket ban, and is also an army rank above colonel.

clue.text: Understanding various things by electric current

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current in physics

indicators.note: various suggests the letters of the word things in a mixed, varied order

explanation.surface: Grasping the workings of assorted gadgets powered by electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges the letters of the word things into NSIGHT; 'by' just places them side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is deep understanding or perception of a situation, a close synonym.

clue.text: Great depression with 'flu widespread

indicators.note: widespread suggests the letters scattered far and wide, rearranged

explanation.surface: A serious slump as an influenza epidemic spreads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'widespread' rearranges the letters of DEPRESSION and FLU.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendiferous is a jokey word for splendid, magnificent, excellent.

clue.text: Approach ladder —- then where to go?

parts.note: a ladder in tights or stockings is a run
on a ladder, the way to go is up

explanation.surface: Someone sets a ladder against a wall and wonders which way to climb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ladder' is not the climbing kind but a RUN in stockings, the British word for a snag in hosiery.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-up is the period or stretch of ground leading up to something, an approach.

clue.text: Urge demon to take citadel by mid-July

parts.note: an imp is a small demon

indicators.note: mid- asks for the middle letters of the word July

parts.note: Sion, a variant spelling of Zion, is the citadel of Jerusalem

explanation.surface: Prodding a devil to capture a fortress by the middle of summer.
explanation.definitionFit: An impulsion is an impelling force or impulse, a noun synonym of an urge.

clue.text: Lacking position, nevertheless

parts.note: lacking something is not being with it
standing is status or position

explanation.surface: Having no status, but carrying on all the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Notwithstanding used as an adverb means in spite of that, all the same.

clue.text: Patience needed to cut round so ereign

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: round means one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: to lance is to cut open, as a boil
the text as held reads so ereign, sovereign with its v lost; ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the sovereign

explanation.surface: Patience is needed to put up with a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text splits sovereign as so ereign; 'round' is the container signal, and ER is the royal cypher of Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerance is forbearance, the patient putting up with others.

clue.text: Party drink: drop lifted for a slug, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means the pieces are read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: a do is a party
port is a fortified wine
to sag is to droop or drop

explanation.surface: At a party a drink is raised, dropped and lands on a slug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' turns the whole run DO PORT SAG upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Slugs and snails are gastropods, molluscs that move on a muscular foot, so a slug is one example.

clue.text: Pretty loud urchin is put out

indicators.note: out means the letters of the words before it are disordered, put out of place

explanation.surface: A noisy street kid is thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of LOUD URCHIN IS PUT, all fifteen of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulchritudinous is a grand, rather ironic word for beautiful, from Latin pulcher, handsome.

clue.text: Passionate in the past, perhaps

parts.note: the past is one grammatical tense

explanation.surface: Someone was passionate once, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks the past as an example of a TENSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense means of extreme strength of feeling, ardent, close to passionate.

clue.text: Support particular type in dairy treatment

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: UHT, ultra-heat treatment, is used to preserve milk
a prig is a fussy, particular kind of person

explanation.surface: Backing a certain strain in how milk is processed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'particular' means fussy, so a PRIG; UHT is the long-life milk process.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright is a vertical post or pillar giving support.

clue.text: Title of male back in trade as member of an inn

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: to barter is to trade goods

indicators.note: back means the title is read in reverse

parts.note: Sir is the title given to a knight

explanation.surface: A knight's title is restored to a tradesman who belongs to a guild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' makes RIS and 'in' is the container signal. The Inns of Court are the London bodies to which every English barrister belongs.
explanation.definitionFit: Every barrister in England and Wales must be a member of one of the four Inns of Court.

clue.text: Man, perhaps, finds uprising good during plot

indicators.note: during means within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot

indicators.note: in a down clue, uprising means the word is read upwards, reversed

parts.note: pi, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for good

explanation.surface: A man is found in a plot to stage a good revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' is not a scheme but a flower bed; 'uprising' turns PI to IP.
explanation.definitionFit: A biped is an animal walking on two legs, and humans are an example.

clue.text: Glower, as politician dismisses leadership

indicators.note: the politician loses its leading letter, its first letter

parts.note: a Member of Parliament is a politician

explanation.surface: An MP scowls at being sacked from the party leadership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glower' looks like a scowl but is read as one that glows.
explanation.definitionFit: An ember is a smouldering coal, literally a thing that glows.

clue.text: African of Cuban-Turkish extraction

indicators.note: extraction means the letters are drawn out of the words, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: An African of Cuban and Turkish descent.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bantu are a large group of peoples of central and southern Africa.

clue.text: Secure relations imbibing good drink

parts.note: to pin something is to fasten it securely

indicators.note: imbibing means taking in, so one piece is drunk into the other

parts.note: kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: Locking in the relatives while they knock back a decent tipple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imbibing' is the container signal, making KGIN; the surface's drinking hides it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pink gin is gin flavoured with Angostura bitters, a classic naval drink.

clue.text: Fully-developed opponents entering ring

indicators.note: entering puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: a ring is a group or clique of people
in bridge, West and North sit as opponents

explanation.surface: Rival boxers climb through the ropes, fully grown men.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North-South partner against East-West, so W and N sit as opponents; 'entering' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Grown-up as an adjective means adult, having reached full development.

clue.text: Stop heading for takeaways!

parts.note: to die is to stop, as an engine does

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, here of takeaways

explanation.surface: An order to quit eating takeaway food.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer too: going on one means a halt to takeaways.
explanation.definitionFit: A diet means cutting out treats, so stopping takeaway meals is what one involves.

clue.text: Killers had set off to get one of four children

indicators.note: off means the letters are set awry and rearranged

parts.note: a quad is a quadruplet, one of four born together

explanation.surface: Murderers set out to snatch one of quadruplets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges the six letters into DEATHS; 'Killers' is the definition, not a hint of murder in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A death squad is a group of assassins sent to kill opponents, so its members are killers.
